title: Ripe Banana Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Puréed ripe banana with brown sugar and lemon stirred into a lighter custard.
summary: A lighter version of our classic custard with puréed very ripe banana, brown sugar and lemon stirred in once cool. Sweet, mellow and fragrant.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Warm the cream, milk, half the sugar and the salt until steaming. Whisk the yolks with the rest of the sugar, pour in two ladles of the hot dairy while whisking, then return everything to the pan; it follows the classic method with less cream.

steps.title: Cook and cool
steps.text: Stir over low heat until it coats the spatula and reads 77-80 °C, without letting it bubble. Sieve into a bowl and cool over the iced water so the banana is not added to a hot base.

steps.title: Purée the banana
steps.text: Mash or blend the bananas with the brown sugar and lemon juice until completely smooth, then whisk into the cooled custard with the vanilla. Lemon slows browning, and the extra sugar keeps the fruit's water from freezing icy.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Press baking paper onto the surface, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn until thick, then freeze for at least 3 h. Banana ice cream is at its best within a week, as the fruit slowly darkens.

tips: Use bananas with plenty of brown speckles; underripe ones taste starchy.
A common mistake is adding the banana to hot custard, which cooks it and dulls the flavour. Cool the custard first.
A pinch of ground cinnamon in the purée is a nice addition.
storage: Freeze covered for up to 1 week. Soften for 5 min before scooping.
